description: Executable task queue for all milestones. Procedure: docs/execution/AUTONOMOUS_WORKFLOW.md. Exactly one milestone is 'active'. A task is READY when its milestone is active, its status is 'todo', its owner is 'worker', and every dependsOn task is 'done'. Workers take the first ready task in array order. Goals of planned milestones are drafts, refined when the owner activates the milestone and its tasks are written. Rationale and blocking decisions per milestone: docs/execution/ROADMAP.md.

milestones.name: Foundation
milestones.goal: A clean monorepo (apps/web Next.js, apps/api NestJS) with working gates (format, lint, typecheck, unit, e2e, build), localization, design tokens, PWA shell, and CI, as defined by ADR-0001. No product features.

milestones.name: App Shell & Design Foundation
milestones.goal: The shared app shell every screen uses (header, main landmark, skip link, language switcher, localized not-found and error states) and the design values it needs, specified and approved by the owner before they are built. No product features.

milestones.name: Backend & Persistence Foundation
milestones.goal: PostgreSQL + Prisma wired into apps/api (ADR-0001 §4a) with a validated DATABASE_URL, a database module, a migration workflow, a local and CI database workflow, and connectivity checks; plus the API contract and validation approach of ADR-0002 (DTOs, global ValidationPipe, one error format, OpenAPI). No product tables (owner decision 2026-10-10). Hosting and data residency stay TBD and do not block M2.

milestones.name: Onboarding + Home
milestones.goal: A new user gets from first open to an invitation to start a diagnostic in three short onboarding steps (exam type, target band) without registering, and a returning user's home answers 'What should I do now?' with one dominant next action and their target band. Guest state stays on the device; no auth, no product tables. Specs, copy, design values and the guest-state and feature-structure ADRs are approved before code.

milestones.name: Reading Engine
milestones.goal: The Reading engine as approved in READING_EXPERIENCE.md: a Reading domain model and content contract, session state with answers kept on the device, the passage-first mobile screen with the question bottom sheet and a full-test navigator, renderers for the approved IELTS question types, highlighting, Pin Evidence, Practice and Exam Modes with timing, and the desktop exam layout, all accessible and tested, with original demo content only. Review, explanations and Error Intelligence are M5. Answer checking and band conversion are M5 (owner, M4-09). Demo content is Academic only; Reading is reached by direct route only, home unchanged.

milestones.name: Reading Review + Error Intelligence
milestones.goal: As approved at M5-01 (owner, 2026-10-11): answer checking for every M4 question type with a raw practice score (no band for the uncalibrated demo test); immutable attempts with answers, pins and highlights kept on the device in write-once entries that are safe across tabs and compatible with M4 data, with result records traceable to their key revision and rules version; evidence-first review of every answer unit with pre-written explanations and 'Explain simpler' in uz/ru/en (AI drafts, reviewed by people before beta); conservatively worded repeated-mistake detection on the first attempt at a test; and retries of questions not fully correct or unanswered. Home unchanged; no runtime AI.

milestones.name: Product UI Foundation + Practice Hub
milestones.goal: The existing product shares one deliberate visual language with owner-approved local reference screenshots; navigation and the responsive shell are settled; a Practice Hub is the clear entry to Reading and later Listening. Not a rewrite: a capped audit list with exit criteria.

milestones.name: Level Check (Diagnostic)
milestones.goal: The real level check replaces the interim page: short original forms, a versioned result model that gives an honestly labelled starting point (no IELTS band while nothing is calibrated), resume and retake, and one next action. Designed for Reading and Listening; the Reading section ships here, the Listening section in M9.

milestones.name: Listening Engine
milestones.goal: Listening as a full engine like M4: Sections 1–4, every Listening question family, the player in Practice and Exam with realistic restrictions, weak-network loading and resume, phone and desktop layouts, a content contract with audio, transcripts and images, original demo audio; plus Reading table, flow-chart and diagram label completion on the shared layouts.

milestones.name: Listening Review + Error Intelligence
milestones.goal: Sourced Listening checking, results and evidence-first review (audio timestamp, evidence replay, transcript excerpt, why, Explain simpler, try again), retries and justified repeated mistakes, the attempt history extended to Listening without losing Reading data, and the level check's Listening section. No runtime AI.

milestones.name: Accounts + Sync
milestones.goal: Optional accounts offered only when they give the learner something; the first server product models; guest-to-account migration and multi-device sync of the device history with its meanings unchanged; deletion and export; legal input on data residency and minors before design.

milestones.name: Cross-skill Home + Progress + Personalization
milestones.goal: Home answers 'what should I do now?' from real level-check, Reading and Listening data with deterministic, explainable rules; a Progress screen without false precision; new-learner, insufficient-data and stale states.

milestones.name: Mock Experience
milestones.goal: Full Listening + Reading mocks with official timing (desktop first), resume rules, calm per-skill results as one measurement, review entry, weak areas, the next action, and history in Progress. No band while content is uncalibrated.

milestones.name: Content System
milestones.goal: A content pipeline across skills: lifecycle and review statuses, provenance and licensing records, difficulty metadata, publishing and rollback, compatibility with historical attempts, authoring tools, and the beta content library drafted with its audio.

milestones.name: PWA + Performance + Reliability
milestones.goal: Final icons and install, the agreed offline scope and caching, service-worker updates, weak-network resilience, performance budgets in CI, error reporting without personal data, and the production environment prepared by the owner.

milestones.name: Beta Hardening
milestones.goal: Every before-beta item done by the right people: legal and privacy, security, accessibility with real TalkBack and iOS checks, human reviews of all keys, evidence and explanations, fluent uz and ru review, provenance review, support and runbooks, then the owner's release approval and launch decision.

The commit transaction (ADR-0009 §4): the finished session written to its `localStorage` entry first; then one read-write transaction over `attempts`, `results` and `firstTry` (strict durability where supported) that keeps an existing attempt unchanged or adds the new one, decides the first-try marker (ADR-0009 §5) and applies retention (20 per test, never the first-try attempt or unknown-schema records); the `localStorage` entry removed only after the transaction has completed and the committed attempt with this id exists; on load, a finished session in `localStorage` is committed, and an in-progress session whose id has a committed attempt is removed
